pages.text: Spodumene, LiAlSi2O6, is the pale pyroxene of the lithium pegmatites. A blast furnace calcines it at about 1,050 °C from alpha to beta-spodumene, which opens to acid where the alpha form will not.
pages.title: Spodumene

pages.text: Two calcined spodumene, 250 mB of sulfuric acid and 500 mB of water, heated, are the acid roast at about 250 °C and the water leach, and give 500 mB of lithium sulfate liquor. Two soda ash in the hot liquor throw down two lithium carbonate, the sodium sulfate staying in solution.
Lithium carbonate is what the trade sells. For the metal it goes to the chloride: two carbonate and 500 mB of hydrochloric acid, heated, give two lithium chloride and 250 mB of carbon dioxide.
pages.title: Carbonate to metal

pages.text: Lithium cannot be won from water, so the dry chloride is electrolysed molten, with potassium chloride in the real bath, at about 450 °C: two chloride on two electrodes in a heated vat give a lithium ingot, half the time three nuggets more, and 250 mB of chlorine.

About a third of the world's lithium comes not from rock but from the brines under the salt flats of Chile, Argentina and Tibet, evaporated in ponds and precipitated with soda ash; there is no such brine in the pack yet.
Sources: Ullmann's Encyclopedia of Industrial Chemistry, "Lithium and Lithium Compounds"; the Talison and Tianqi spodumene flowsheets; USGS, Mineral Commodity Summaries 2025, Lithium.
